output:
VERDICT: FAIL

- [CRITICAL] `classify()` treats unknown/unparseable age as old: `Number.isFinite(p.ageMs) ? p.ageMs : Infinity`. On Windows, a missing or unparsable `CreationDate` becomes `ageMs: Infinity`, so the age gate passes despite ambiguity. Fix: require `Number.isFinite(p.ageMs) && p.ageMs >= minAgeMs`; otherwise skip.

- [CRITICAL] `--min-age-ms` can disable the age gate. `parseInt()` can produce `NaN`, and `minAgeMs = NaN` makes `p.ageMs < minAgeMs` false for every process. A low value like `0` also violates the stated 20-minute safety contract. Fix: validate finite integer and clamp to `ORPHAN_MIN_AGE_MS`, or reject invalid/lower values.

- [CRITICAL] No revalidation before `terminate(o.pid)`. Between classify and kill, the PID can exit and be reused by a fresh legitimate process; the reaper will still SIGTERM/taskkill that PID. Fix: store an identity token from enumeration, such as Windows `CreationDate` or POSIX `/proc/<pid>/stat` start time, then immediately re-enumerate and re-run all gates against the same PID/start-time/cmd/ppid before signaling.

- [HIGH] `liveLockPids()` fails unsafe for this contract. On any lock enumeration/parse error it returns an empty set, so `--apply` can reap a process that actually has a fresh lock. The contract says any enumeration/parse/tooling error must reap nothing. Fix: make lock-state failure explicit and cause `run()` to return zero orphans.

- [HIGH] Signature matching is overbroad: `isDispatchProc()` uses substring checks like `c.includes("dispatch-agent.js")` and `c.includes("WARPOS_RUN_ID")`. A foreign orphan process with those strings in an argument can be killed. Fix: parse argv/executable structurally; require a known provider executable plus a trusted WarpOS dispatch marker, or require wrapper script paths resolved under `ROOT`.

- [HIGH] POSIX process enumeration is line-oriented and can be spoofed if `ps` renders embedded newlines in argv. A crafted command line could inject a fake row such as `0 1 999999 WARPOS_RUN_ID`, and `terminate(0)` would call `process.kill(0, "SIGTERM")`, signaling the whole process group. Fix: never parse `ps args` as authoritative rows; read `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` NUL-delimited where available, and reject `pid <= 1` before classification and termination.

- [MEDIUM] `terminate(pid)` does not validate PID range/type. Even aside from enumeration spoofing, `pid=0` has dangerous POSIX semantics. Fix: require `Number.isSafeInteger(pid) && pid > 1 && pid !== process.pid` before any signal/taskkill.

- [MEDIUM] “Own process tree” exclusion only covers self and ancestors via `selfTree()`, not descendants. The parent-alive gate usually prevents killing descendants, but it is not the stated full tree exclusion. Fix: compute descendants from the snapshot as well, and skip all ancestors plus descendants.

- [LOW] Windows tools are invoked by basename: `powershell.exe` and `taskkill`. This is not shell injection, and `taskkill` is called without `/F`, but absolute system paths reduce PATH/current-directory hijack risk. Fix: resolve to trusted System32/Sysnative paths.

- [LOW] `taskkill /T` expands the blast radius to descendants of the matched PID. That may be intended, but after any misclassification or PID reuse it increases damage. Fix: only use `/T` after identity revalidation, or make tree termination an explicit second-stage option.
